title: Recording takes: everything played once
summary: No retakes; they rehearsed beforehand and played each number straight through.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Did you, excuse me, did you make a lot of takes on each tune or did you just play it once?

We didn't, we didn't lose no time at all. You just went and played it, like when you made the orange curl trombone. You just play it once? We didn't have just played like we generally do play it and then, all right, let's cut, let's try this and over.
No. We played them numbers right on.
We played those numbers right on through. I don't remember playing none of them numbers over.

even with the singers? The singers, no, we played them because we rehearsed them right there 12th and Central and the music was out there, you know, spikes was placed. And you were all, everything down, all we went right and set up and played them. It wasn't like you go there like they do now, you make a record and say, let's take another one, let's try this one. You never didn't know what you were doing, no? I was playing there, I never knew what I was doing. Couldn't tell, you know. Yeah.
